skill.name: prompting
skill.description: Create and optimize AI prompts using clear structure, concise instructions, focused context, concrete examples, and explicit constraints.
skill.summary: Practical standards for writing clear, efficient prompts and agent instructions.
skill.author: AaronAbuUsama

security_audit.summary: The only static finding is a false positive caused by Markdown inline-code delimiters around a local documentation reference. The reviewed files contain prompt-writing guidance and no executable code, malicious instructions, or semantic security concerns.

finding_verdicts.reason: The backticks delimit inline Markdown around a local documentation reference; they are not Ruby or shell execution syntax in an executable file. No runnable command is present.

content.value_statement: Vague or overloaded prompts reduce model accuracy and waste context. This skill structures and optimizes prompts with direct instructions, focused context, examples, and constraints.
actual_capabilities: Creates prompts with clear background, instructions, examples, and constraints.
Optimizes existing prompts by removing redundancy and replacing vague language.
Identifies missing structure, unclear requirements, and unnecessary context.
Applies progressive discovery and just-in-time context loading principles.
Guides prompt review, testing, comparison, and iterative refinement.
limitations: Does not execute prompts or verify model outputs automatically.
Does not calculate token counts without support from the host tool.
Provides general standards rather than domain-specific factual expertise.
References a supplementary local file that may be unavailable outside the original environment.

use_cases.title: Draft reliable task prompts
use_cases.description: Turn a goal, audience, output format, and constraints into a concise structured prompt.

use_cases.title: Refine agent instructions
use_cases.description: Reduce noise and clarify tool use, context boundaries, examples, and success criteria.

use_cases.title: Standardize team prompts
use_cases.description: Apply a consistent review checklist across shared prompts and agent configurations.

prompt_templates.title: Create a basic prompt
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a prompt for [task]. The desired output is [format], the audience is [audience], and these constraints apply: [constraints].
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when starting from a clear goal with a few known requirements.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize an existing prompt
prompt_templates.prompt: Optimize the prompt below for clarity and efficiency. Remove redundancy, replace vague language, add useful sections, and preserve every essential requirement. Prompt: [prompt]
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when a prompt is verbose, unclear, or poorly structured.

prompt_templates.title: Design agent instructions
prompt_templates.prompt: Design instructions for an agent that must [goal]. Define essential context, allowed tools, decision rules, examples, constraints, and measurable success criteria.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when an AI agent needs repeatable behavior and clear operating boundaries.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a complex agent prompt
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this multi-step agent prompt for ambiguity, context overload, conflicting instructions, premature data loading, and weak success criteria. Provide findings, a revision, and a test plan.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for advanced prompts that coordinate tools, context, and multiple stages.

output_examples.input: Create a prompt that summarizes a weekly project update for executives.
output: Background: Summarize a weekly project update for executive readers.
Instructions: Return five bullets covering progress, risks, decisions, metrics, and next steps.
Constraints: Use plain language. Keep each bullet under 20 words.

output_examples.input: Improve this instruction: Please look at this report and maybe tell me what seems important.
output: Review the report and identify the five most important findings.
For each finding, state its evidence, business impact, and recommended action.
Separate confirmed facts from assumptions. Do not add unsupported conclusions.

best_practices: State the desired outcome, audience, format, and success criteria.
Separate essential context, instructions, examples, and constraints into clear sections.
Test prompts with representative inputs and refine them using observed results.
anti_patterns: Do not include historical context that does not affect the requested output.
Do not use vague suggestions when a direct, testable instruction is possible.
Do not load full data sets before the task requires their details.

faq.question: What types of prompts can this skill improve?
faq.answer: It supports task prompts, agent instructions, tool guidance, context plans, and other structured LLM requests.

faq.question: Does this skill work with Claude and Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. Its model-independent principles apply to Claude, Codex, Claude Code, and other instruction-following models.

faq.question: Can it create a prompt from a simple goal?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide the goal, audience, output format, essential context, and constraints for the strongest result.

faq.question: Can it optimize an existing prompt?
faq.answer: Yes. It can identify redundancy, vague wording, missing structure, context overload, and unclear success criteria.

faq.question: Does it test prompt performance automatically?
faq.answer: No. It recommends testing and iteration, but the user or host environment must run and evaluate the prompt.

faq.question: Does it provide domain-specific facts?
faq.answer: No. It improves prompt structure and context use but does not replace qualified domain knowledge or source verification.
